decision.trend: Research has been focused on designing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved ductility, strength, and thermal stability. Earlier studies have explored the effects of different alloying elements, processing techniques, and microstructural features on the mechanical properties of HEAs. Recent studies have demonstrated the potential of HEAs to exhibit high ductility and strength, particularly when processed using advanced techniques such as laser powder bed fusion or high-pressure and high-temperature treatment.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made, there is still a lack of understanding of the underlying mechanisms that control the ductility of HEAs, and further research is needed to develop a comprehensive framework for designing HEAs with optimized mechanical properties.
decision.why: The next step would be to investigate the effects of high-pressure and high-temperature treatment on the microstructure and mechanical properties of HEAs, building on the recent study (PMC11087546) that demonstrated the potential of this technique to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in eutectic high entropy alloys.
